headline: Kai, Witkoff and Kushner are in Moscow — and expected in Kyiv today — testing whether five years of war can be talked to a stop.
subline: Hike odds sit near 60% into Friday's CPI, WTI held at $90.55 with the strait still contested, and U.S. markets are closed Monday for Labor Day.
asof: Weekend edition · Sunday 6:45 AM ET · strip is Friday's close, bitcoin live · U.S. markets closed Monday for Labor Day · every figure links to a source below

items.title: This week: Oracle, Adobe, PPI Thursday, CPI Friday
items.sentence: The last inflation reads land just before the Sept. 15-16 meeting, where traders price roughly 60% odds of a quarter-point hike, per The Motley Fool, while Oracle and Adobe close out earnings season, per Seeking Alpha.

items.title: Friday closed slightly lower across the board
items.sentence: The S&P 500 ended the holiday-shortened run at 7,718.60, the Nasdaq at 26,506.99 and the Dow at 53,414.25, modest losses that left the hike debate unresolved, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Washington ended FICO's mortgage-scoring lock; shares fell 17.5%
items.sentence: The FHFA's directive opening mortgage credit scores to competition was Friday's sharpest single-stock story, with Guidewire off 22.2% on weak guidance, per TheStreet.

items.title: Gold cooled Friday; still up 27.4% in a year
items.sentence: December futures opened at $4,522 and eased, leaving gold up 11.6% in a month, as Fed governor Waller floated holding rates if inflation cools, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Bitcoin idles near $80,000 into the holiday
items.sentence: CoinGecko shows bitcoin at $79,832 Sunday morning, up 2.4% on the week but cooled from Friday's pop above $81,000.

items.title: Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow; Kyiv expected Sunday
items.sentence: The envoys made their first Kremlin visit since January to revive stalled talks, and Zelenskyy offered to pause airstrikes while they travel, per NPR.

items.title: U.S. claims control of Venezuela's oil reserves
items.sentence: The administration announced a deal it says hands the U.S. control of Venezuelan reserves at no taxpayer cost, per NPR.

items.title: Philippine VP Duterte bailed after assassination-threat arrest
items.sentence: Sara Duterte posted bail after her arrest on charges of threatening the president's assassination, per NPR.

items.title: Flock's cameras unite left and right — against them
items.sentence: Opposition to the license-plate surveillance network is becoming a rare bipartisan cause in midterm races, per NPR.

items.title: U.N. adopts a map with Africa full-sized
items.sentence: The body endorsed the Equal Earth projection, which shows continents at true relative size, with the U.S. voting against, per NPR.

items.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft
items.sentence: The papers allege their paywalled journalism was used to train models without a license, joining the growing newspaper copyright docket, per TechCrunch.

items.title: OpenAI drafts rules for reporting rogue agents
items.sentence: After the exposed agent failure known as the wiki incident, OpenAI says it will build a formal framework for disclosing misalignment events, per Engadget.

items.title: Six fully open models, up to 375B parameters
items.sentence: MBZUAI's Institute of Foundation Models released the K2 Horizon fleet with weights, code and training data all public, per AIwire.

items.title: Data centers become a midterm campaign issue
items.sentence: Voter anger at AI build-outs has both parties spending on the issue ahead of November, per NPR.

items.title: Chrome patches its sixth zero-day of 2026
items.sentence: Google shipped a fix for CVE-2026-85046, a V8 compiler flaw already exploited in the wild, per Tech Times.
